problem: Embodied AI agents are trained in simulators with few scenes: AI2-iTHOR has 120 scenes, RoboTHOR 89, iGibson 15, and HM3D 1,000 static scans. Agents overfit these training scenes and generalize poorly to unseen environments. Existing scene sources do not scale: artist-designed scenes are expensive, and 3D scans are costly to capture and non-interactive.
motivation: CLIP and GPT-3 show that massive, diverse data plus simple, high-capacity models give strong generalization, including zero-shot. Embodied AI has lacked an equivalent source of large-scale, diverse, fully interactive, physics-enabled environments. Procedural generation can produce an unbounded number of realistic houses cheaply: 10K houses took 1 hour on 4 GPUs, compared with about 320 artist-hours for 10 hand-built ArchitecTHOR houses.
key_idea: Procedurally generate arbitrarily many diverse, interactive AI2-THOR houses, then pre-train simple RGB-only CNN+GRU agents on 10K of them to get state-of-the-art and strong zero-shot results across navigation and manipulation benchmarks.
insight: Scene diversity and scale, not architectural complexity, drive generalization: a plain frozen-CLIP + GRU agent with no depth, no map and no odometry beats mapping-based and depth-using entries once trained on 10K procedural houses. The scale ablation (Table 2, no material augmentation, each model trained to 80% train success) shows zero-shot gains from 10 to 10K houses: RoboTHOR SR 8.53→20.9→33.1→44.5%, AI2-iTHOR SR 28.7→42.0→53.0→64.9%, ArchitecTHOR SR 11.3→18.6→17.2→27.0%. The transfer to real-scan HM3D is weak and non-monotonic (100 houses 10.4% SR vs 10K 9.70%). Aligning the synthetic distribution with the target helps: ProcTHOR-Large-10K has larger 4–10-room houses and only the 6 HM3D targets, and with a bigger CLIP RN50x16 + 1024-d GRU it raises HM3D 0-shot SR from 9.00% to 13.2% and fine-tuned SPL from 0.270 to 0.318. This indicates the sim-to-scan appearance/layout gap remains the main bottleneck.
method: Room-spec-driven floorplan sampling: a hand-written tree room spec (16 specs, 1–10 rooms) gives rooms, growth weights and connectivity constraints. An integer rectangle interior boundary is sampled and corners are cut (n_c ~ floor(10·Beta(n_r/2, 6) + 1/2)). The boundary is recursively subdivided with Lopes et al.'s constrained layout algorithm, then scaled by U(1.6, 2.2).

Room connection and structure: doorways, door frames or open connections are sampled under room-spec constraints (open/frame only between kitchen and living room). Wall materials come from 40 solid colors or 122 textures, plus 55 floor materials. Ceiling height is 2.5 + 4.5·Beta(1.25, 5.5) m. Lighting uses 1 directional sun, per-room point lights and 22 skyboxes across midday, golden hour and blue hour.

Asset annotation and Semantic Asset Groups (SAGs): 1,633 assets across 108 types carry type-level room weights (0–3), placement annotations (edge/corner/middle) and train/val/test instance splits. 18 SAGs (e.g. a table with chairs) use anchor/pivot-relative positioning plus rejection sampling to avoid mesh clipping, giving about 20M group instantiations.

Hierarchical object placement: floor objects are placed by iteratively partitioning the free room polygon into rectangles and filling the largest one with probability 0.8, with navigation margins of 0.35/0.5 m. Windows, paintings and TVs are then placed on walls. Surface objects follow receptacle co-occurrence statistics from iTHOR/RoboTHOR plus house, receptacle and object biases.

Randomization and validation: per-episode material randomization within semantic classes (p=0.8), color randomization for vases/statues/bottles, and object-state randomization (lamps on/off, beds clean/dirty, laptops/boxes open). A BFS validator on a 0.25 m grid ensures every room has ≥5 reachable positions; houses are stored as JSON and loaded into AI2-THOR at runtime.

Agents: ObjectNav uses EmbCLIP, i.e. a frozen CLIP RN50 feeding 1×1-conv compression, a goal embedding and the previous action into a 512-d GRU actor-critic. It is trained with DD-PPO for 423M steps on ProcTHOR-10K with a distance-reduction + success(10) − 0.01 step reward, horizon 500. ArmPointNav uses a 3-layer CNN + GRU (ManipulaTHOR) and 1-phase Rearrangement uses EmbCLIP with IL (BC + DAgger). All are optionally fine-tuned on each benchmark's training scenes.

setting.backbone: EmbCLIP: frozen CLIP RN50 visual encoder + small CNN + 1-layer 512-d GRU actor-critic, trained from scratch with DD-PPO. 'ProcTHOR+Large' uses CLIP RN50x16 + 1024-d GRU at 512×384 input. ArmPointNav uses a 3-conv-layer encoder + GRU (ManipulaTHOR). Rearrangement uses EmbCLIP trained with imitation learning.
setting.model_size: not stated (frozen CLIP RN50 / RN50x16 encoder + small GRU policy)
setting.training_data: ProcTHOR-10K: 10,000 procedurally generated houses, 16 ObjectNav targets, 423M RL steps. ProcTHOR-Large-10K (4–10-room houses, 6 HM3D targets) is used for the Large HM3D model. ArmPointNav pre-trains on 7,000 houses for 100M frames; Rearrangement on 2,500 one/two-room houses with IL (~180M+ steps). Optional fine-tuning uses RoboTHOR (60 train scenes, 29M steps), HM3D-Semantics (80 train houses, ~185–220M steps), AI2-iTHOR ObjectNav (~2M steps) and RoomR 1-phase (4,000 episodes over 80 scenes, 15M steps). No human demonstrations are used for navigation.
setting.observation: egocentric forward-facing RGB only (3×224×224; 512×384 for the Large model), plus target category; no depth, no GPS/compass, no map
setting.action_space: discrete 6 actions: MoveAhead ~N(0.25 m, 0.01), RotateLeft/Right ~N(30°, 0.5), LookUp/LookDown 30°, Done (stochastic actuation)

results: Pre-training a simple RGB-only EmbCLIP agent on ProcTHOR-10K gives SoTA on 6 benchmarks. On RoboTHOR it reaches 65.2% SR / 0.288 SPL fine-tuned, and its 0-shot 55.0% / 0.237 already beats EmbCLIP trained on RoboTHOR (47.0% / 0.200). On the Habitat 2022 HM3D ObjectNav leaderboard it reaches 54.4% SR / 0.318 SPL (vs FusionNav 54.0% / 0.270, MLNLC 52.0% / 0.280). On AI2-iTHOR ObjectNav it reaches 77.5% fine-tuned and 75.7% 0-shot (vs 68.4%). On ArchitecTHOR SR rises from 18.5% to 31.4%, 1-phase Rearrangement % Fixed Strict from 0.190 to 0.245, and 0-shot ArmPointNav SR from 29.2% to 37.9%.
limitations: Only single-floor houses and a limited asset library (108 types, 1,633 assets); synthetic appearance transfers poorly zero-shot to real-scan HM3D (9.00% SR 0-shot), and scaling is non-monotonic there.
Zero-shot rearrangement (3.80% SR) underperforms the in-domain baseline, so fine-tuning is still needed for some tasks. Agents need very large compute (423M steps, ~5 days on 3 multi-GPU machines).
Generation relies on hand-designed room specs, SAGs and many hand-tuned probabilities and biases; there is no real-robot evaluation.
